the kernel-log scan is token-aware (see `nic_signatures`): the substring match it replaced counted the `e1000` inside the kernel's own `RAMDISK: [mem 0x07ee1000-0x07ffffff]` line — the initrd's load address, which moves whenever the initrd is rebuilt — and failed this case on a guest with no NIC. `_case_nic_signature_scan` pins both halves of the fix, deterministically.

cases.name: the NIC-signature scan reads names, not addresses (a regression case)
cases.vector: deterministic fixtures, no VM: `RAMDISK: [mem 0x07ee1000-0x07ffffff]` (the initrd's load address, which moves whenever the initrd is rebuilt) must not count as `e1000`, while a driver banner, a device probe line and the standalone forms of the other signatures must

notes: the scan is token-aware (a signature embedded in a longer alphanumeric run does not count): a NIC, a NIC driver or a net device prints its name as a token of its own, while the guest's kernel log prints physical addresses. The live case above still asserts the guest's own kernel log carries none of them.

findings.title: no egress allowlist exists to test
findings.detail: the persona's egress-denial surface assumes an egress proxy (decision 0010 names one for a later milestone). In this MVP the only wire is the per-VM UDS muxer, so the suite asserts the structural equivalent (only the created listeners exist, no AF_VSOCK, no NIC) instead of a denial that cannot occur
